JSON flattened to CSV with pandas (scratch flatten.py).
full_dataset_size: Repo: data/ fixtures ~320 MB (329 files), pip package 'edgartools' a few MB. Underlying SEC EDGAR: companyfacts JSON per filer (ABNB ~5-8 MB, all tags/all filings), Financial Statement Data Sets ~50-100 MB per quarter zip since 2009, full-index of every filing since 1993 (millions of rows); unlimited but rate-limited to 10 req/s.
description: edgartools is an MIT Python client that turns SEC EDGAR (filings index, XBRL companyfacts/companyconcept/frames, 13F, Forms 3/4/5, 8-K items) into pandas objects with no key beyond a User-Agent string. The sample is one row per XBRL fact per filing (grain: entity x tag x period x accession, with the 'filed' date, so every value is point-in-time) plus one row per filing in the submissions index. Source is data.sec.gov directly; the library only wraps it. An analyst would use it to build vintage-correct quarterly panels for ABNB and peers (BKNG, EXPE, MAR, HLT) and the cruise-line customer-deposit series (NCLH/CCL/RCL ContractWithCustomerLiability) as the book-ahead analogue to Airbnb's unearned fees, and to pull 13F/Form 4 history for ABNB.
issues: The job card's tag names 404 on data.sec.gov (ABNB does not file us-gaap:Revenues; NCLH does not file DeferredRevenueCurrent) - working tags are RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax and ContractWithCustomerLiabilityCurrent; ABNB itself reports both ContractWithCustomerLiability and DeferredRevenueCurrent (seen in companyfacts head). 'git sparse-checkout set README.md data examples' fails because README.md is a file; use 'set examples data' (README is checked out anyway). data/ is 320 MB of test fixtures (Apple, Netflix, 13F XML samples), not ABNB data - not copied. No licence concern: MIT code, SEC data public domain; SEC asks for a real contact in User-Agent and <=10 req/s. companyfacts head is a 5 MB truncation (not valid JSON), used only to list tags. Restated values appear as duplicate (end, val) rows across accessions; the dedupe/vintage rule is the analyst's choice.
